description.text: Giovanni Gualberto was born around 985 into the noble Visdomini family at the castle of Poggio Petroio.  As a youth he was more interested in vanity and romantic intrigues than in religion, but the murder of his older brother Ugo set him on a path of vengeance.  On a Good Friday he encountered the man who had killed his brother in a narrow lane of Florence; the killer begged for mercy in the name of Jesus, and Gualberto, moved by the day’s significance, granted him clemency and abandoned his revenge.

After this act of mercy he entered the Benedictine community at San Miniato al Monte, where he began a life of strict penance and humility.  He later left the order to found the Vallumbrosan Order in 1036, establishing a monastery at Vallombrosa that emphasized austere communal living and the cultivation of trees rather than a traditional garden.  His compassion for the poor and ill earned him the esteem of several popes, and he was canonized by Pope Celestine III on 24 October 1193.

curiosities.text: Gualberto is the patron saint of foresters, park rangers, and forests, a role formalized by Pope Pius XII in 1951 for the Italian Forest Corps and by the Brazilian Church in 1957.
At Vallombrosa he chose to plant firs and pines instead of a conventional garden, reflecting his commitment to a simple, nature‑oriented monastic life.
He was canonized by Pope Celestine III on 24 October 1193, more than a century after his death, and his feast day was later added to the General Roman Calendar in 1595 before being removed in 1969.
